children: Indian refiners plan monthly purchases of propane and butane as imports continue to meet a large share of domestic LPG demand

Indian state-owned LPG importers have floated a joint tender to source around 2.75 million metric tonnes of liquefied petroleum gas from the United States for delivery throughout 2027, according to a tender document reviewed by Reuters on Friday.

Indian Oil, Bharat Petroleum and Hindustan Petroleum are seeking four very large gas carrier cargoes every month, with each cargo carrying around 46,000 tonnes. The cargoes will be evenly split between propane and butane and supplied on a delivered basis during 2027.

The tender also seeks one 45,000-tonne cargo every month on a free-on-board basis, according to the document. The tender is valid until October 22, with the proposed procurement covering regular supplies across the whole of 2027.

LPG is a mixture of propane and butane and is widely used as cooking fuel in Indian households. India is the world’s second-largest LPG importer after China and relies significantly on overseas supplies to meet domestic consumption.

India imported 21.85 million metric tonnes of LPG in 2025, with about 90 per cent of those imports sourced from the Middle East, government data showed. Imported LPG accounted for around 66 per cent of the country’s total LPG consumption during the year.

The proposed US procurement would provide Indian state-owned companies with an additional source of LPG outside their traditional Middle Eastern supply base. The monthly cargo requirement also indicates an effort to secure supplies for an extended period.

India’s dependence on imported LPG came under pressure after the US-Israeli war on Iran began at the end of February, causing severe disruption to fuel supplies. The disruption prompted the government to take measures to protect LPG availability for households.

In March, the Indian government invoked emergency measures to divert petrochemical feedstocks from industry towards households. The move came as households continued to rely on LPG as a major cooking fuel.
The latest tender seeks substantial US-origin LPG volumes for 2027 as Indian state-owned importers look to secure supplies amid the disruptions that have affected fuel markets.
